_meta.description: Credited, freely licensed images for battles in data/battles.json (Historian, c02b4d0). Metadata only, plus 320 px Commons thumbnail URLs; no image files are stored.
_meta.keys: Exact ids from data/battles.json. BCE years use a double hyphen ('kerma--1500' = 1500 BCE). war_id is read from data/battles.json / db/wars.json (both read-only).
_meta.licence_policy: PD, CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA, or Flickr Commons no known restrictions. Licence read from the Commons API extmetadata on 2026-10-25. Every file, page and thumb URL returned HTTP 200 that day.
_meta.evidence_type_note: primary-account = contemporary official or participant maps/plans. Period illustrations made after the event are dated by the image date.

excluded.File:MahdistsvsEthiopians.png: CC0 here is the uploader's dedication of a photo of an Ethiopian painting (1935, artist unknown). The artwork's own status is unverified.
excluded.File:Storming Ferkeh.jpg: Commons date of 1895 is before the battle of 1896; not resolved.
excluded.File:Ali Dinar.jpg: Photo of a corpse taken as a trophy. Excluded on dignity grounds even though the PD claim is plausible.
excluded.File:ALKHALIFA ABD ALLAH DEATH.jpg: An 1899 photo with an uploader CC BY-SA 4.0 tag and no clear author, so the licence is unreliable. It is also a death photo.
excluded.File:Church of the Granite Columns 2007-: Commons has no author or date metadata, so a credit cannot be verified.
excluded.File:EzanaGreekTablet.jpg: Commons credits a Flickr user, but the description is mixed; a duplicate of Ezana evidence already covered.
excluded.File:Dongola Throne Hall.jpg: A crop of a Flickr CC BY-SA 2.0 photo that is credited on Commons as "own work", so the attribution is inconsistent.

_meta.post1956_check: 2026-10-25: none of the 17 ids in db/battles_post1956.json (fa486bd) are keyed here (clashes: none); no images were added for them, and none for war-2023.
_meta.alt_ar_note: alt_ar = working Arabic translation of each image's English description (the alt that b.json uses), Map Designer 2026-10-26, tagged [يحتاج تحقق]. Internal until reviewed. null where the description is empty.

kerma--593.description: This is a well preserved victory stela which was erected by Pharaoh Psamtik II of the 26th Saite dynasty (c.592 BC) at Kalabsha when he returned from campaigning in Nubia. image: A tent in a wooded area. A soldier with a moustache is sitting under the shade of the tent. Two others are sitting
